title: Instruction Encoding Bit Builder
description: A 32-bit Thumb-2 bit grid for VFMA.F32, colored by encoding bit field, built live from three register selectors, hand-editable bit by bit, with a disassembler that decodes the result back.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Assembly Language
Computer Architecture
chapter_title: Beyond the Assembler: Hand-Encoding and Instruction Formats

educational.topic: Hand-encoding a Thumb-2 floating-point instruction and verifying it
learningObjectives: Construct a 32-bit machine word from encoding-table bit-field positions
Calculate the split V and low-bit encoding of a single-precision register
Verify a hand-encoded word by disassembling it back
prerequisites: An instruction is a number the processor interprets
Thumb-2 instructions are one or two 16-bit halfwords

controls.label: Assemble word
controls.purpose: Rebuild the canonical encoding and discard hand edits

controls.label: Disassemble
controls.purpose: Decode the current word back to a mnemonic and operands

controls.label: Flip one random bit
controls.purpose: Corrupt a single bit to show that the result still decodes

controls.label: Bit cell
controls.purpose: Toggle any individual bit by hand

simulationModel.modelType: Bidirectional encoder and disassembler for the ARMv8-M floating-point three-register instruction space
equations: Vx = x >> 1 and low bit = x & 1 for a single-precision register Sx
mnemonic is selected by bit 23, bits 21-20 and bit 6
assumptions: Registers are limited to s0-s7 so every field fits on screen
Single precision only; sz = 1 is detected on decode but not fully named
The condition field is 1110, as it always is for 32-bit Thumb
limitations: Covers the three-register floating-point space only, not the whole VFP encoding
Does not model the IT-block conditional forms of these instructions

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Construct on paper, verify in the simulation, then break deliberately and observe that nothing complains
keyQuestions: Which bits hold the destination register?
What happens to a program containing a hand-encoded word with one wrong bit?
commonMisconceptions: That a wrong bit pattern will fail to assemble or fail to run
That the disassembly check is a formality
assessmentOpportunities: Encode VFMA.F32 s5, s3, s6 by hand and check against the simulation
Describe how to diagnose a plausible-looking wrong FFT result
